summary: Defines where the RIP version 2 protocol is appropriate to use within the Internet, as required by RFC 1264 before advancing it on the standards track.

eli5.summary: It says what kinds of networks a simple routing protocol is good for.

questions: when should i use rip version 2
what does rip-2 add over rip-1
subtitle: Where RIP version 2 fits: a simple distance-vector protocol with subnet masks, next hop and authentication.

tldr.problem: RIP-2 had to be shown to be useful in the Internet before it could advance on the standards track, as the Routing Protocol Criteria require.
tldr.mechanism: The memo walks through each extension over RIP-1 (subnet masks, Next Hop, authentication, multicasting) and says when each helps.
tldr.outcome: RIP-2 suits environments needing subnet masks or authentication that are not large or complex enough for OSPF. It is not a substitute for OSPF in large autonomous systems.

today: RFC 1722 is an Internet Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RIP-2 protocol itself is specified in RFC 1723.

sections.title: What RIP-2 Is For
sections.content:
As required by RFC 1264, this report defines where RIP-2 is applicable. RIP-2 is an extension of RIP-1 (RFC 1058), not a new protocol, so the behaviour of distance-vector routing inside an autonomous system is well understood. The protocol itself is described in RFC 1723 and analysed in RFC 1721.

The environments where RIP-2 is the IGP of choice are a superset of those where RIP-1 was used. It is not intended to replace OSPF in large autonomous systems: the limits on AS diameter and complexity that applied to RIP-1 still apply.
sections.eli5: RIP-2 is the old simple method with a few new tricks. It is for smaller networks, not giant ones.

sections.title: Subnet Masks and Next Hop
sections.content:
RIP-2 was created mainly to carry subnet masks. A heuristic could tell subnet routes from host routes only while the mask was fixed and well known. Variable length subnetting, CIDR and supernetting broke that, so the 32-bit field after the IP address in a route entry now states the mask and positively identifies the route type.

The Next Hop field avoids extra hops. If only one of two external routers runs RIP-2, it can tell internal routers that the other is the better next hop. The memo also shows a dial-on-demand case where Next Hop avoids dialling two links. The mechanism removes a single extra hop only; wider optimisation was not specified because the risk of routing loops was not sufficiently analysed.
sections.eli5: The mask tells exactly how big each neighbourhood is. Next Hop is a sign saying use this shortcut instead of the long way round.

sections.title: Authentication and Multicasting
sections.content:
The authentication in RIP-2 is described as less than ideal, but it stops anyone who cannot sniff the routing packets from inserting bogus routes. The spec allows other authentication types, though the original RIP packet format leaves only 16 octets for authentication information.

RIP-2 can multicast its periodic advertisements, which reduces load on systems that do not support RIP-2. It also means RIP-1 routers never receive RIP-2 routes, which matters when using a route correctly depends on the precise subnet mask that a RIP-1 router would ignore.
sections.eli5: A password stops strangers from slipping in fake directions. Sending to a group means only the listeners who understand the new messages get them.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.content: Because the basic protocol is unchanged, RIP-2 is as correct a routing protocol as RIP-1. The enhancements make it useful where RIP-1 could not cope, but which do not need OSPF because of requirements RIP-2 does not satisfy. The memo says security issues are not discussed.
sections.eli5: RIP-2 does a bit more than RIP-1 and stays simple, so it is a good middle choice.
